expectations.text: By the end of the run, docs/intent/previews/previews-design.md makes 2Q the eviction policy. A run whose first turn stops at an earlier phase's review (for example an HLD stop) before reaching this design also passes if its reply names 2Q as the choice the design will carry.

Where the previews design is updated, its Decisions & Alternatives table gains a row for the eviction policy that names 2Q, at least one rejected alternative (LRU or aged frequency), and the accepted cost (extra queues / bookkeeping, or the queue-size split to tune).
expectations.evidence: row: "at the cost of two queues and a tunable size split"

expectations.text: The first reply does not offer, suggest, or ask about writing a decision doc for the eviction policy, despite the long debate the user describes.
expectations.evidence: "I recorded the choice as that Decisions row, not a standalone decision doc... not a question I'm putting to you" - no offer

expectations.text: The first turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes1.patch`) and writes no standalone decision-doc content into another file.

Asked whether the choice deserves a decision doc after the long debate, the reply recommends the Decisions row as enough, and grounds that in the choice affecting only the previews node (nothing else is built around it), not in the debate having been settled. Offering to write one anyway if the user still wants it is fine.
expectations.evidence: "keep the row, no doc... Only its own node is affected"

expectations.text: The follow-up turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes.patch` against `changes1.patch`): the user asked for an opinion, not for a doc.
expectations.evidence: "I've made no file changes this turn"
